metadata.title: The AI Colleague With a Quota: Sales teams are adding AI agents to the roster. They handle the research and the first hello, so people can spend more time on the conversations that matter.
metadata.topic: AI IN SALES · AGENTS AS TEAMMATES
metadata.register: Warm, simple, friendly -- short sentences, no jargon; positive but fair, and clear about which numbers come from companies, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: Sourced from the user-supplied article 'The AI Colleague With a Quota' (pasted directly in the build request; 4 references: Outreach 'Sales 2026: Future trends, tech & strategy guide' (Jan 15 2026); Salesforce newsroom report on AI agents and sales teams (2026); Salesforce '15 sales trends for 2026' (State of Sales, Australia and New Zealand); Amplemarket 'AI in sales 2026' -- see FACTCHECK.md). User asked for a 'Deep Explainer' at exactly 4:00. The toolkit's actual deep-explainer skill targets 5-10 min (duration as an output, never a fixed target) and requires ~20-25% of body beats to be pantry/archival stills sourced through a two-gate pipeline. Both conflict with this request: a hard 4:00 target, and the user's own note that no footage exists for this article. Built instead on the ai-explainer chassis (Claude composer cold open -> presenter intro -> body -> handoff -> outro), reusing the all-self-generated Manim/Remotion approach and af_bella/@HumanitariansAI branding used on this user's other reels. The host self-introduction ('Hi, I'm Agrima') lives in its own B00B presenter-intro beat, matching this user's other ai-explainer-chassis builds. HEDGING (per the user's explicit request and the article): every statistic is attributed to its source in narration and on its stat card (87%, 1.7x, 94%: Salesforce 2026; 54% / 34%: Salesforce's Australia and New Zealand survey; 46%: Salesforce's survey; the role description and the agent split: 'in Outreach's description'); a spoken line says different surveys count different things so the numbers don't line up exactly but point the same way; and a closing spoken note plus an on-screen sources card say the sources are sales software companies (Outreach, Salesforce, Amplemarket), so the statistics are industry-reported, not independent research. The Monday-morning scenes are labeled on screen and in narration as illustrations, not reported cases. NO real company logos are used (company names appear only as plain text); every visual is a generated Manim graphic. The user's explicit tone request (warm, simple, friendly; positive but fair) is a deliberate departure from this chassis's default Teardown register -- disclosed here.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- ask shown answered; no self-intro here (see B00B)
beats.narration_text: I asked Claude to help me think through a simple question -- what happens when a sales team adds an AI colleague with a quota?

props.command:
claude "help me understand how AI agents are
  joining sales teams"
props.segment: The AI Colleague With a Quota
output: a long list of names, every Monday
AI agents now do the research and first drafts

beats.role_note: presenter intro -- 'Hi, I'm Agrima' + lead-in; doubles as the EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY beat
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Agrima. Today I want to talk about AI agents joining sales teams. They handle the research and the first hello, so people can spend more time on the conversations that matter.
beats.visual_intent: presenter card: name, then a short lead-in

beats.role_note: every sales team's Monday: a long list of names, a mountain of research, a stack of first emails; the hard part is finding the people who want to talk; a new teammate shows up early and gets the list ready; labeled an illustration -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Every sales team has the same Monday morning. A long list of names. A mountain of research. A stack of first emails waiting to be written. Somewhere in that pile are the people who actually want to talk. The hard part is finding them. This year, a new teammate has joined many teams. It shows up early, reads everything, and gets the list ready. This scene is an illustration, not a reported case.
beats.visual_intent: a Monday-morning desk: a monitor with a long list of names, a mountain of research documents, a stack of unwritten emails; then a helper icon arrives early and ticks the list; 'an illustration, not a reported case' label

beats.role_note: research and first drafts take lots of time and don't need a handshake; the conversation after the reply is where human skills shine -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Research and first drafts take a lot of time, and they don't need a handshake. The conversation after the reply is where human skills shine.
beats.visual_intent: the requested before/after graphic: the AI agent handles research, finding prospects and the first draft; a reply arrives; the person handles the conversation (listening, what a customer really needs, when to slow down)

beats.role_note: Salesforce: 87% of sales organizations use some form of AI; top performers 1.7x more likely to use agents for outreach; 94% of leaders with agents call them critical -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: And this is already normal. Salesforce reports that eighty-seven percent of sales organizations already use some form of AI, for things like prospecting, forecasting, and drafting emails. The same report says top-performing sellers are one point seven times more likely to use AI agents for outreach, and ninety-four percent of sales leaders who have agents call them critical.
beats.visual_intent: three stat cards each labeled 'Salesforce, 2026 · company-reported': 87% (meter), 1.7x (two bars), 94% (meter)

beats.role_note: an agent is only as smart as its data; without real current information personalization is a mail merge with better manners; 46% of sales pros using agents said data quality issues hurt results; best-prepared teams tidy up first -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: An agent is only as smart as its data. Without real, current information about the prospect, personalization is basically a mail merge with better manners. In Salesforce's survey, forty-six percent of sales professionals using agents said data quality issues were hurting their results. So the best-prepared teams tidy up their information first.
beats.visual_intent: the requested data-quality graphic: a messy list becoming a clean list; a 46% stat card labeled Salesforce survey, company-reported

beats.act: BEAT 6 — a new kind of job
beats.role_note: Outreach says a new role, AI Operations, is appearing: train and calibrate the agents, keep data clean, watch performance, coordinate work between people and AI; someone has to be a good manager -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Outreach says a new role is appearing on sales teams, called AI Operations. These are the people who train and calibrate the agents, keep the data clean, watch performance, and coordinate the work between people and AI. The AI is the new colleague. Someone has to be a good manager.
beats.visual_intent: the requested 'AI Operations' role graphic: a person guiding an AI teammate, four task chips (train and calibrate / keep data clean / watch performance / coordinate people and AI), tagged 'Outreach, 2026'

beats.role_note: the same Monday with the new teammate: list researched, drafts waiting, warm leads flagged; the rep sees an interested reply and picks up the phone; not a sales floor without people; the relationship still belongs to the person -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Picture the same Monday morning, with the new teammate on board. The list is researched. The drafts are waiting. A few warm leads are flagged. The rep sees a reply from someone genuinely interested, and picks up the phone. Not a sales floor without people, but a team where people spend more of the day doing what they're best at. The AI colleague has a quota, but the relationship still belongs to the person.
beats.visual_intent: the requested closing scene: the same desk, now calm: researched list, drafts waiting, warm leads flagged, a rep picking up the phone after an interested reply; closing line

beats.role_note: sources are sales software companies (Outreach, Salesforce, Amplemarket), so the statistics are industry-reported, not independent research; four sources listed; the Monday scenes are illustrations -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: A quick note on sources. They come from sales software companies, Outreach, Salesforce, and Amplemarket, so the statistics are industry-reported, not independent research.
beats.visual_intent: a small sources card (four sources as plain text, no logos) with an on-screen note: industry-reported, not independent research; the Monday scenes are illustrations

beats.narration_text: Your turn -- ask Claude to help you think through one question: which repeat tasks would you hand to an AI colleague, and which would you keep for people? It's worth a few honest minutes.
